correctness.rationale: The exactly defined Petersen graph yields 59049 spin states, independently enumerated in two different decompositions. Exact bundled rational convex coefficients prove all 36 nonnegative-magnetization sector minima lie above a seven-branch envelope for all real anisotropies and fields; seven rational witnesses prove strict phase exposure. Exact critical counts are 30 and 21, with analytic spin reversal extending to negative fields. The certificate and both standalone programs were actually executed.

evidence: A known zero-field Ising result on generalized Petersen GP(n,2) specializes at n=5 to exchange minimum -9 and ten fully occupied spin configurations (five at magnetization +2, five at -2). This is an already-covered subcase, not claimed as new in isolation.

Zaslavsky (2012) relates frustration indices to the maximum-cut problem in an all-negative signed Petersen graph; that controls the spin-1/2 all-occupied slice but not the variable-occupancy crystal-field envelope.
Kimel et al. 1992 uses a square lattice; Yang et al. 2007 uses an interacting quantum spin-one chain and nonmagnetic hole decomposition.

The Petersen line graph and the Petersen graph are distinct graphs with respectively fifteen and ten spin sites.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the unique ten-vertex cubic girth-five cage and a standard frustrated network. Its classical spin-one extension with a neutral spin variable has a natural but not previously identified exact two-field occupancy/magnetization classification. The distinct weak-field seven-branch diagram and the 10-to-6-to-zero vacancy cascade, including magnetization collapse and coexistence degeneracies, form a complete reproducible finite frustrated-magnetic benchmark, not an arbitrary unmotivated graph slice. No downstream bulk or general-graph theorem is claimed.
